title: Enterprise Onboarding — Support, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures, checklists, and reference material for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It combines: the enterprise onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation/playbook steps, known issues and workarounds, ongoing health checks, and QBR (Quarterly Business Review) templates. This document is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and the customer SO/Platform teams.

Audience
- Customer Success (CSM)
- Solutions Engineering (SE)
- Support / Escalation Engineers
- Customer Platform / SRE contacts

Goals
- Provide a single reference for a repeatable, low-friction enterprise onboarding.
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-inference (target: < 2 weeks for standard integrations).
- Define clear escalation paths and SLAs to meet enterprise reliability expectations.
- Establish health metrics and QBR templates for long-term success.

Ownership and Contacts
| Role | Team | Primary Contact | Secondary Contact |
|------|------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Playbook Owner | Customer Success | Avery Chen | Samir Patel |
| Integration Lead | Solutions Engineering | Lena Ortiz | Kai Nguyen |
| Escalation Lead | Support Engineering | Marcus Li | Priya Kapoor |
| Product / Runtime Owner | Eng — Serving Runtime | Nisha Rao | Tomas Becker |

Onboarding Milestones (high level)
1. Discovery (0–3 days)
   1.1. Collect product goals, expected traffic patterns, compliance requirements, and regulatory constraints.
   1.2. Identify contact roster and on-call rotations.
2. Integration + PoC (3–10 days)
   2.1. Provide quickstart template and API keys (dev sandbox).
   2.2. Implement authentication, request throttling, and basic observability hooks.
   2.3. Run smoke tests and confirm model parity.
3. Performance tuning & SLA alignment (7–14 days)
   3.1. Define latency, throughput, and error SLOs.
   3.2. Apply batching/quantization recommendations and KV prefix caching settings.
4. Production cutover (day determined by customer)
   4.1. Canary rollout, monitoring, and rollback plan.
5. QBR readiness & handoff to success (30–90 days)
   5.1. Establish recurring QBR cadence and KPIs.

Detailed Integration Guide (summary)
- Supported endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank.
- Authentication: API key header Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>.
- Example request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_API_KEY}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-v2", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize quarterly revenue"}], "max_tokens":256}'

- Webhooks / callbacks (recommended for async workloads)
  - Configure a public HTTPS endpoint (TLS 1.2+). Use HMAC signature header X-Redwood-Sig to validate.
  - Example webhook validation (pseudo):
    const computed = hmac_sha256(secret, body);
    if (computed !== request.headers['x-redwood-sig']) reject(401);

- Integration checklist (technical)
  - Verify TLS and MTLS (if required).
  - Provision dedicated keys for team members.
  - Enable request/response logging (PII filtered) for first 14 days.
  - Add tracing hooks (X-Request-ID).
  - Configure rate limits and test burst scenarios.

Escalation Playbook
Severities and target response times (enterprise tier):
- P0 / Critical (service down, customer-facing outage): initial response <= 15 minutes, target mitigation within 2 hours.
- P1 / Major (severe degradation impacting production): initial response <= 1 hour, mitigation within 4 hours.
- P2 / Moderate (partial impact, degraded performance): initial response <= 4 hours, mitigation within 24 hours.
- P3 / Minor (configuration questions, non-urgent bugs): response within 2 business days.

Escalation path (ordered):
1. Customer CSM -> Support Tier 1 (email + ticket).
2. Support Tier 1 triage -> Support Tier 2 (SE/Integration) if reproduction or deep config required.
3. Support Tier 2 -> Escalation Lead (Marcus Li) for P1/P0.
4. Escalation Lead -> Runtime on-call (see internal roster) for infrastructure or model-serving issues.
5. If security-sensitive: also notify Security (security-and-compliance@redwood.example).

Escalation playbook steps (numbered)
1. Triage and reproduce: gather request id, timestamps, full request payload (redact PII), and a HAR trace if relevant.
2. Confirm scope: single-customer, single-route, or global.
3. Apply temporary mitigation: route to a fallback model variant or increase dedicated capacity (if available).
4. Root cause analysis (post-mitigation) and timeline to fix.
5. Customer communication: status updates every 30 minutes for P0, hourly for P1.

Ticket template (to be included in support UI)
- Title: [P1] <short description> — <customer-name>
- Fields: Severity, Affected Routes, Example Request ID, Timestamp, Steps to Reproduce, Primary Contact, Business Impact, Temporary Mitigations Tried

Known Issues and Workarounds (select list)
1. Symptom: High p99 latency for long context (>= 8k tokens).
   Root cause: Attention kernel mismatch for long-sequence paths on some GPU kernels.
   Workaround: Route requests to long-sequence-optimized model variant (model-redwood-long) and enable prefix-KV caching.
2. Symptom: Occasional 5xx errors during high burst traffic.
   Root cause: Autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration causing transient queue overflow.
   Workaround: Increase burst capacity and apply temporary rate limiting on client side; file follow-up infra ticket to adjust cooldown to 30s.
3. Symptom: Small hallucination regression after model rollout.
   Root cause: Prompt-formatting differences and tokenization changes.
   Workaround: Revert to previous stable model, capture prompt set, open model-quality regression ticket with Applied ML.

Health Checks and KPIs (to monitor continuously)
- Availability: API uptime (target >= 99.95% monthly for enterprise).
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for /chat and /generate (target p95 < 350ms for small prompts).
- Error rate: 5xx rate < 0.1% for enterprise routes.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec relative to committed capacity.
- Cost KPIs: avg cost per 1k tokens and per-request cost variance.
- Quality: eval regressions per release (alerts if > 2% regression on critical prompt set).

Sample monitoring queries (Prometheus/PromQL style)
- P95 latency for chat (last 5m): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=\"/chat\"}[5m])) by (le))
- 5xx rate (last 1h): sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\"}[1h])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1h]))

QBR Template and Agenda
- Cadence: Quarterly or by customer agreement.
- Required attendees: CSM, Customer Engineering Lead, SE, Product (as needed).
- Standard agenda:
  1. Executive summary + success highlights (5m)
  2. Adoption and usage trends (tokens, active routes, growth) (10m)
  3. Reliability & incidents (SLO adherence, incidents since last QBR) (10m)
  4. Cost and efficiency (batching, cache hit rates, recommendations) (10m)
  5. Roadmap and upcoming releases (model upgrades, infra changes) (10m)
  6. Action items and ownership (5m)

QBR Data Pack (deliver 48h before meeting)
- 90 / 30 / 7 day usage summary (tokens, requests, error rates)
- Model performance benchmarks and any regressions on the customer prompt set
- Recommendations: batching, caching, model-variant changes, cost-savings opportunities

Production Cutover and Rollback Plan (checklist)
- Pre-cutover
  - Confirm runbook, on-call availability, and communication channels (Slack #cs-<customer>, status page pre-provision).
  - Run load test at production scale in staging.
  - Ensure canary route is in place with traffic split (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Cutover day
  - Monitor health dashboards for first 2 hours intensively.
  - Keep rollback decision authority with the customer CSM + Escalation Lead.
- Rollback steps
  1. Re-route traffic to previous stable model or dedicated pool.
  2. Revoke recently applied config changes.
  3. Open RCA ticket and schedule postmortem if rollback triggered by incident.

Communication Templates
- P0 template (short):
  Subject: [P0] API outage affecting <customer> — immediate mitigation in progress
  Body: Short summary, steps taken, ETA for mitigation, next update time.
- Post-incident RCA template (detailed):
  - Incident summary, timeline, root cause, impact, mitigation, long-term fix, action owners, ETA.

Review Cadence and Maintenance
- Playbook owner (Avery Chen) will review quarterly and after any P0/P1 incident.
- Major updates (process or SLA changes) require approval from Customer Success leadership and reviewers listed above.
